entry.title: Kubernetes CI: Lease Test Mailboxes, Don't Retry Blindly
entry.summary: Email verification tests become unreliable when the mailbox is treated like an ordinary HTTP dependency. A pipeline sends a message, waits a few seconds, sees nothing, and retries. The retry may create a duplicate message, race the first delivery, or consume a mailbox that another test owns. In Kubernetes CI, the cleaner model is an inbox lease: one test run reserves one isolated mailbox for a bounded period, records that ownership, and releases it whether the test passes or fails. This turns a vague polling problem into a resource-lifecycle problem that can be operated. Most email assertions have at least four separate steps: Create or reserve a test mailbox. Trigger the application event. Wait for the message to arrive and identify the right message. Release the mailbox and retain enough…

entry.title: Rate Limiting Like Gandalf: Building a Distributed Cache with Redis
entry.summary:
The Quest Begins (The "Why")
Ever had your API melt down because a sudden traffic spike hammered every endpoint at once? I remember a late‑night deploy where our “simple” in‑process counter crashed under a flash sale, and the pager started singing like a busted karaoke machine. We needed a way to throttle requests without turning every service into a bottleneck or rewriting the whole stack. The problem boiled down to: how do we share a counter across many instances, keep it fast, and survive node failures? A naïve approach—each service keeps its own local counter—fails the moment you scale beyond one node. A centralized DB works but adds latency that kills throughput.
